faqs.a:
(a)
All connected water services will be metered by the installation of water meters of
               the style and type as set forth in the schedule of materials issued by the engineering
               division in accordance with city standard specifications and drawings. Each meter
               and its service line from the main to the meter will be the same size as the connection
               to the city main, unless the utilities manager determines otherwise.
(b)
Every residential and nonresidential facility shall have a separate service line and
               meter from the city main to the building except in such circumstances as set forth
               in
section 102-33
.
(c)
The first and original meter will be purchased by the owner and become a part of the
               property served. This meter will be used to measure water use during construction,
               and, subsequently, the water delivered to the user.
(d)
The city shall have reasonable access to the meter for the purpose of reading and
               servicing. The city may remove or exchange the meter for purposes of testing and servicing.
(e)
The cost of normal servicing, repairing, and replacement of water meters will be paid
               by the city. The cost of repairs resulting from abuse, freezing, hot water, or other
               causes will be paid by the user.
(f)
Water meters cannot be installed in driveways, sidewalks, or parking lots except upon
               prior written authorization from the utilities manager. If there is no alternative
               location, then heavy duty round meter pit ring and lids shall be used as specified
               in city engineering specifications. All costs associated with relocating or upgrading
               existing meter pits to heavy duty shall be at the user's expense.
(g)
The meter flow accuracy limits shall be determined by the city in accordance with
               industry standards as set forth in "Water Meters—Selection, Installation, Testing,
               and Maintenance" (AWWA M6), third edition, copyright 1986 by the American Water Works
               Association, which is hereby adopted by reference.
(h)
It is unlawful for any person to interfere with or remove a water meter from any service
               connection without first obtaining the written approval of the department of utilities.
               Whenever any meter is removed with such approval, the meter will be immediately returned
               to the department of utilities. In the event that a meter is missing from a location
               where it is known that a meter had previously been installed, the owner of the premises
               is required to install a new meter and pay all costs for such installation.
(i)
Water service lines to all residential dwellings for fire protection will be metered.
               The owner will furnish engineering calculations to the department of utilities substantiating
               the fire flow and domestic flow requirements. The system development charge will be
               based on the domestic flow requirement and not the fire flow requirement. The meter
               will be installed as previously set forth in this section. The fire line will be installed
               as required in the Engineering Code of Standards and Specifications, as amended.
(j)
Should the city perform any work or incur any expense for the installation, removal,
               replacement, servicing, relocation, or maintenance of any water meter, appurtenance,
               or meter pit, and any such work or expense is determined to be the responsibility
               by either the user or the owner, the city is authorized to recover the actual cost
               of such work or expense as provided in
section 102-41
.
(k)
Water service lines to commercial swimming pools, including the supporting facilities,
               such as the bath or club house, and mechanical room, shall be metered. Water meters
               will be installed in the water service lines at the following locations:
(1)
For seasonal and nonseasonal swimming pool installations where no water is delivered
               to irrigate the landscaping on the property, then only one water meter will be installed
               at the property line in accordance with
section 102-61
(c).
(2)
For seasonal and nonseasonal swimming pool installations where water is also delivered
               to irrigate landscaping on the property, in addition to the first water meter required
               in accordance with
section 102-61
(c), a second water meter will be installed in the water service line immediately
               ahead of the swimming pool and supporting facilities.
(3)
For seasonal and nonseasonal swimming pool installations serving multi-family residential
               facilities, with or without water being delivered to irrigate landscaping on the property,
               in addition to the first water meter required in accordance with
section 102-37
(c), a second water meter shall be installed in the water service line immediately
               ahead of the swimming pool and supporting facilities.
(l)
All the water and sewer service lines to a multifamily residential facility shall
               be installed downstream of the master meter pit on the building or subdivision property.
               Each water service line branch to each unit in the building shall have a curb stop
               valve.
(m)
The water meter in an inactive connected water service will be removed by the city.
